products.name: Strawberry Matcha
products.tagline: A strawberry latte with a matcha backbone.
products.description:
Culinary matcha sifted with freeze-dried strawberry and real vanilla bean, then sweetened lightly with stevia leaf and monk fruit. Whisk a spoonful into a splash of hot water, pour in steamed or cold milk, and it turns a soft pistachio-pink.

The strawberry comes through first and the green tea follows, grassy and a little sweet, with vanilla rounding off the finish. It's a morning cup that feels like a treat without being a dessert.
products.inTheCup: Creamy strawberry over grassy, slightly sweet green tea, with a soft vanilla finish. The latte turns a soft pistachio-pink.

hot.note: Whisk until smooth, then add 6 oz of steamed milk.

iced.note: Whisk into cold water and pour over milk and ice.

products.serveWith: Milk is essential: dairy, oat, or coconut. Extra sweetener is optional.

products.name: Blackberry Oolong
products.tagline: Jammy blackberry on toasted, honeyed oolong.
products.description:
A medium-roast oolong blended with freeze-dried blackberries, blackberry leaf, elderberries, and a little lemon peel. The oolong brings a toasted honey note, the berries bring the jam, and the finish is dry and a little wine-like.

It pours amber-gold with a ruby tint from the elderberry. Oolong is made to be steeped more than once, so keep the leaves: the second cup is softer and rounder than the first.
products.inTheCup: Jammy dark berry over toasted honey, with a dry, slightly wine-like finish. Amber-gold with a ruby tint.

hot.note: Steeps two or three times. Add a minute each time.

products.serveWith: A thin lemon slice brightens the berry. A little honey is good. Skip cream.

products.name: Cran-Pom
products.tagline: Tart cranberry and pomegranate, hot, iced, or mulled.
products.description:
Hibiscus and rosehips make a deep ruby base for freeze-dried cranberries, pomegranate arils, apple, and orange peel. It's tart and juicy, with a round body that comes from the same fruit as our cranberry-pomegranate wine.

This is the year-round blend. Brew it double strength over ice in summer. In winter, simmer it with a cinnamon stick and an orange slice and it becomes a mulled cup that fills the kitchen.
products.inTheCup: Tart, juicy cranberry and red fruit with a round, slightly wine-like body. Deep ruby red.

hot.note: For mulled, simmer 10 minutes with a cinnamon stick and an orange slice.

iced.note: Brew double strength and pour over ice.

products.serveWith: Best a little sweet. An orange or lemon wedge is good. Never add cream: the acid curdles it.

products.name: Unwind
products.tagline: Tulsi, rose, and orange peel, warm and gently spiced.
products.description:
Kapoor tulsi and lemon balm with rose petals, orange peel, and a few cracked cardamom pods. Tulsi has a clove-like sweetness, the rose stays soft in the background, and the orange lifts the whole cup.

Nº 1 is the blend for the end of the workday: the kettle on, the laptop closed, nothing else asked of you for a while. Steep it covered so the aroma stays in the cup.
products.inTheCup: Gently spicy and sweet, with clove-like tulsi, soft rose, and a citrus lift. Pale gold with a faint blush.
products.serveWith: A little honey. Lemon is fine. No cream.

products.name: Lights Out
products.tagline: Linden and mint, honeyed and floral.
products.description:
Linden leaf and flower, passionflower, spearmint, and oat straw, with a little lavender and lemon verbena. It brews pale straw-gold and tastes honeyed and floral, with a cool mint finish.

This is the last cup of the day, made after the dishes are done and the house has gone quiet. Steep it covered for seven to ten minutes; the longer steep brings out more of the linden.
products.inTheCup: Soft, honeyed floral, with a cool mint finish and a faint lemon note. Pale straw gold.
cautions: Contains passionflower. Talk to your doctor before drinking if you take sedatives or sleep medication.
products.serveWith: Honey suits it best. No lemon or cream.

products.name: Cinnamon Apple
products.tagline: Apple pie in a mug, no sugar.
products.description:
Ceylon black tea with broken apple chips, cassia cinnamon, and cracked cardamom, sweetened with stevia leaf. It smells like a pie cooling on the counter and tastes like the crust: baked apple, warm cinnamon, and a brisk, clean finish.

It's the tea version of our cinnamon apple wine. It takes milk well, so try it as a latte on a cold morning. Keep the steep under five minutes, or the black tea turns bitter.
products.inTheCup: Apple-pie crust, warm cinnamon, and a brisk, clean finish. Bright copper-amber.

hot.note: Past 5 minutes the black tea turns bitter.

products.serveWith: Cream or milk works well, and so does honey or brown sugar. Skip lemon.

products.name: Chicory Chai
products.tagline: Dark, roasty, and spiced. No coffee, no caffeine.
products.description:
Roasted chicory and dandelion root give this blend the dark, roasty body of coffee. Cinnamon, ginger, cardamom, clove, and cracked black pepper make it a chai, and a little apple softens the edges.

It's the cup for coffee drinkers who want a second mug without the caffeine. Brew it strong and add milk, or simmer it in half milk, half water for a stovetop latte.
products.inTheCup: Dark and roasty like coffee, with warm spice and a peppery finish. Deep brown, close to black coffee.

hot.note: Strain well. For a latte, simmer 5 minutes in half water, half milk.

products.serveWith: Milk and a little sweetener bring out the best in it. Skip lemon.

products.name: Hearth
products.tagline: Rooibos, pear, and vanilla, like dessert by the fire.
products.description:
Rooibos and chamomile with freeze-dried pear, chopped vanilla bean, and a little ginger. It brews honey-amber with a red-orange glow and tastes round and honeyed, with soft pear and vanilla and just enough ginger to warm the finish.

Nº 2 is made for a blanket and a long evening. Rooibos never turns bitter, so you can let it steep while you settle in. It's also very good with a splash of warm milk.
products.inTheCup: Honeyed and round, with soft pear and vanilla and a gentle ginger warmth. Honey-amber with a red-orange glow.

hot.note: Rooibos doesn't turn bitter, so a longer steep is fine.

products.serveWith: Milk or cream works well, and so does honey. Skip lemon.

products.name: Amaretto
products.tagline: Marzipan and apricot over malty black tea.
products.description:
Black tea misted with pure almond extract, then blended with apricot, a little roasted chicory, and chopped vanilla bean. It tastes like marzipan and stone fruit over a malty base, with a light roasted finish.

This is our winter dessert tea, and it's at its best with cream. Contains almond flavoring.
products.inTheCup: Marzipan and stone fruit over a malty base, with a light roasted finish. Copper-amber.
products.serveWith: Cream is excellent, and so is sugar or honey. Skip lemon.

products.name: Gold
products.tagline: Honeybush and orange blossom, with saffron on the side.
products.description:
Honeybush, chamomile, orange blossom, lemon peel, and calendula petals, packed with a separate vial of saffron threads. Drop a few threads into each cup and it glows a clear golden yellow, with honey and soft florals over the saffron's warm, hay-like depth.

Nº 5 is our holiday gift tin, made for slow mornings in December. Let the threads soak in a little hot water for five minutes before adding the tea if you want even more color.
products.inTheCup: Honey and soft florals with a hay-like warmth from the saffron. A clear, glowing golden yellow.
cautions: Contains saffron. Not recommended during pregnancy.

hot.measure: about 1 heaping tbsp, plus 5–6 saffron threads

products.serveWith: A little honey. No cream or lemon, which hide the saffron.

products.name: Forest
products.tagline: Cacao and chaga, dark and earthy, in easy sachets.
products.description:
Cacao husk and wild chaga form the base, with roasted dandelion root, lion's mane, cordyceps, cinnamon, vanilla bean, and a little orange peel. It brews deep mahogany and tastes of dark chocolate and earth, with a savory depth and a soft vanilla-cinnamon finish.

Forest comes in sachets because chaga likes a long steep. Give it ten minutes, or simmer it for fifteen on a snowy afternoon. It re-steeps well, too.
products.inTheCup: Dark chocolate and earth, with a savory, broth-like depth and a soft vanilla-cinnamon finish. Deep mahogany brown.
cautions: Contains chaga. Talk to your doctor before drinking if you take blood thinners or diabetes medication, or have a history of kidney stones.

hot.note: Or simmer 15 minutes for a deeper cup. Re-steeps well.

products.serveWith: Oat milk is great, and honey or maple syrup works well. Skip lemon.

products.name: Blueberry Lemonade
products.tagline: Pours blue, turns violet when you add lemon.
products.description:
Delicate white tea with freeze-dried blueberries, lemon peel, lemongrass, and butterfly pea flower. It brews a deep blue, then turns violet-purple the moment you squeeze in lemon.

It tastes like soft berry and bright citrus over a light, slightly sweet tea. Cold-brew it overnight in the fridge for the smoothest glass, and keep the water under a boil if you brew it hot, because white tea turns bitter in very hot water.
products.inTheCup: Soft berry and bright citrus over a delicate, slightly sweet tea. Deep blue, turning violet with lemon.

hot.note: Hotter water turns white tea bitter.

iced.note: Cold-brew 6 to 8 hours in the fridge.

products.serveWith: Lemon, which is the point, and a little sweetener. No cream.

products.name: Shade
products.tagline: Mint, lemon verbena, and elderflower, made for iced.
products.description:
Peppermint, lemon verbena, and lemon balm, finished with elderflower. It's cool and green, with a bright lemon lift and a soft floral finish, and it pours a pale green-gold.

Nº 4 is the porch tea: cold-brewed overnight and poured over ice on the first hot afternoon of the year. Cold-brewing makes the mint sweeter and softer. It's good hot, too.
products.inTheCup: Cool and green, with a bright lemon lift and a soft, floral elderflower finish. Pale green-gold.

iced.note: Cold-brew 8 hours in the fridge, or brew double strength and pour over ice.

products.serveWith: A lemon slice is fine, and a little honey. No cream.
